results.proposal_summary: The Nature for Health (N4H) Phase II Expression of Interest, funded by Germany's BMUV through the International Climate Initiative (IKI) with an initial contribution of €50 million, invites governments of ODA-eligible countries to apply for seed funding of up to USD 2,250,000 per proposal to implement integrated, preventative One Health approaches addressing the environmental determinants of health, including pandemic prevention through upstream zoonotic spillover reduction. Eligible applicants are exclusively government entities (national and sub-national) and regional intergovernmental entities representing multiple member states from OECD DAC-listed countries; non-governmental entities are explicitly excluded. The call covers ODA-eligible countries and territories worldwide. The application window was open from 10 January to 7 April 2025, with Phase II partners selected in August 2025. Implementation spans 2-3 years following a scoping phase. The ILO is ineligible as a non-governmental entity, and the call deadline has passed.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses on biodiversity, One Health, and pandemic prevention through environmental determinants of health — themes with minimal overlap with the ILO's core mandate of labour standards, employment, social protection, and decent work.

results.proposal_summary: The Africa Disaster Risk Financing Programme (ADRiFi), managed by the African Development Bank (AfDB) in partnership with the African Risk Capacity (ARC) Group, is a multi-donor initiative established in 2018 to enhance resilience to climate shocks across African Regional Member Countries. The ADRiFi Multi-Donor Trust Fund (MDTF), established in 2021 with approximately USD 96.7 million in contributions from Canada, Switzerland, Norway, Netherlands, United Kingdom, and the United States, provides premium subsidies and capacity development support to enable eligible African governments to access climate disaster risk insurance. The programme is aimed exclusively at African sovereign governments (Regional Member Countries), which access support by submitting formal requests to the Bank and meeting ARC risk pool participation requirements. The page is a general programme description with no current open call for proposals, no application deadline, and no specific funding round, rendering it ineligible as an active CfP.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the programme touches on social protection and livelihoods of vulnerable populations (including women in agriculture), its core mechanism is disaster risk financing through climate insurance for national governments, which is outside ILO's mandate as a technical assistance and labour standards agency.

results.proposal_summary: The African Development Bank launched the African Emergency Food Production Facility, a $1.5 billion initiative in response to food supply disruptions caused by the Russia-Ukraine war, which created a shortfall of at least 30 million tonnes of food in Africa. The facility aims to provide certified seeds and fertilizers to 20 million African smallholder farmers to rapidly produce 38 million additional tonnes of food, representing a $12 billion increase in food production over two years. The page is an informational programme description published in May 2022 and last updated July 2022; it does not constitute an open Call for Proposals, contains no application mechanism, no eligibility criteria for applicant organisations, and no submission deadline.
results.ilo_match_evidence: This initiative focuses on emergency agricultural food production and input supply to smallholder farmers in Africa, which falls outside the ILO's core mandate of labour standards, employment policy, social protection, and decent work.

results.proposal_summary: The Africa Fertilizer Financing Mechanism (AFFM) is a special fund administered by the African Development Bank Group, established by African Union member states to provide innovative financing solutions — primarily credit guarantees and grants — to improve fertilizer production, procurement, and distribution across African Regional Member Countries. The mechanism operates through three strategic pillars: access to finance for fertilizer value chains, policy reform support, and facilitation of smallholder farmers' access to inputs and technical assistance. This page is an informational landing page, not an active Call for Proposals; no application window, submission deadline, or open CfP is present. Past projects have ranged from USD 2 million to USD 10.3 million across countries including Kenya, Uganda, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, and Nigeria.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The AFFM is an agricultural financing mechanism focused on fertilizer supply chains and private-sector investment mobilisation, with minimal overlap with ILO's mandate on labour standards, decent work, social protection, or employment policy.

results.proposal_summary: The African Green Banks Initiative (AGBI) is an African Development Bank-led pan-African programme aimed at creating an ecosystem of green banks throughout Africa to mobilise climate finance for green and sustainable growth, with a target of $1.5 billion in green investment facilities by 2030. Operating through two windows — Technical Assistance and a Green Finance Facility — the initiative uses a blended finance approach to leverage private and public sector investments in support of African countries' NDCs. results.proposal_summary: The U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor (DRL) is offering a single cooperative agreement award of USD 2,959,500 under NOFO DFOP0019659 to promote responsible investment and rights-respecting production models. results.proposal_summary: The Common Fund for Commodities (CFC) has launched its 29th Call for Proposals under the theme 'Thriving Farmers, Resilient Ecosystems, Empowered Communities', seeking applications from SMEs, cooperatives, social enterprises, NGOs, and public or private sector entities based in or operating in any of its 101 member countries. The CFC provides financing exclusively through loans and debt instruments (not grants), with a maximum of USD 1.5 million for regular projects and up to USD 300,000 under its Fast-Track procedure. Priority areas include trade finance, regenerative agriculture, local value addition, agtech, financial access for smallholders, and women's entrepreneurship; the CFC particularly encourages proposals from the Congo Basin region and Least Developed Countries. Applicants must have at least 3 years of operational history. The submission deadline is 1 October 2026, and application forms must be submitted in English.
